name: Regimental moustache

lead: The regimental moustache is a trimmed moustache associated with military service, in particular the British Army tradition in which soldiers wore one as part of the uniform. It is kept neat and tidy rather than ornate.
People grow one to add definition to the upper face, to sharpen the area under the nose and above the lip, and for the disciplined, traditional look the style carries.

paras: It is grown on the upper lip and kept trimmed to a regular shape, in a groomed, uniform style, with regular trimming and often a comb or small scissors.

Little beyond ordinary grooming issues such as skin irritation. The cultural associations vary by place and era, and some military moustache styles carry historical baggage, such as the toothbrush shape after the 1930s.

Defines the area above the lip and under the nose
angle.text: A trimmed moustache gives the lower face a defined line and a formal, military character. Its look depends on regular upkeep and on matching its width to the mouth and face.

lead: A regimental moustache is a neat, military-style moustache. Until 1916, enlisted soldiers in the British Army were not allowed to shave the upper lip, so a moustache was effectively part of the uniform [1].

As a grooming choice, it adds facial hair structure above the lip while leaving the cheeks and chin clean-shaven or lightly trimmed, and it is associated with a disciplined, traditional image. Historian Susan Walton links the Victorian revival of facial hair to efforts to present the army around manly virtues [1].

Moustaches were especially fashionable in the West in the 1880s and 1890s, and military moustache traditions continue in several armies, from armour and cavalry units in the US to regiments of the Indian Army [1].

paras: The moustache was a defining trait of the British soldier, and enlisted men could not shave the upper lip until 1916 [1]. Moustaches then remained common among soldiers, including during the Falklands Campaign [1]. Military moustaches peaked in fashion in the 1880s and 1890s [1].

Styles associated with the military include the handlebar and imperial, with upturned ends; the kaiser, long, waxed and curled; the horseshoe; the walrus; and the short toothbrush, whose association with Hitler made it unpopular afterward [1]. In India the Abhinandan moustache became a trend in 2019 after Wing Commander Abhinandan Varthaman [1].

timeline.event: Military moustaches at peak fashion in the West [1].
